title: Quiche Lorraine
subtitle: Open pastry tart with smoked bacon and custard filling
excerpt: A crisp shortcrust pastry case filled with a silky custard of eggs and double cream, studded with lardons. The original and still the best of all quiches.

recipe.sourceNotes: Quiche Lorraine comes from the region of Lorraine in north-eastern France and is one of the most copied French dishes in the world. The original does not contain cheese: the authentic Lorraine is bacon and custard only. Gruyère was added later in the Swiss and Alsatian versions and has become standard in the French-inspired quiches of Britain and America. The word quiche derives from the German Kuchen, cake, and the dish reflects the historically contested Alsace-Lorraine region's mixed French and German food traditions.

content.text: Blind-bake the pastry case before adding the filling: this prevents the dreaded soggy bottom. The pastry must be fully cooked through: dry and beginning to colour at the edges, rather than merely pale and set, before the custard goes in. The custard filling should wobble in the centre when you take it out of the oven: it will continue to set as it cools. If you bake it until it is firm in the oven, it will be rubbery by the time it is eaten.

Make the pastry: rub the cold butter into the flour until it resembles fine crumbs. Add the egg and ice water and bring together into a dough. Do not overwork. Wrap in cling film and rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. Roll the pastry to 3 mm thick on a floured surface. Line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Trim the edges and prick the base. Line with baking paper and fill with baking beans. Blind-bake for 20 minutes, then remove the paper and beans and bake for a further 10 minutes until the pastry is dry and lightly golden. Remove from the oven and reduce the temperature to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3.
Fry the lardons in a dry pan for 5 minutes until golden. Scatter evenly over the base of the pastry case.

Whisk together the eggs, cream, milk, salt, white pepper, and nutmeg. Pour slowly over the lardons. The tart tin should be placed on a baking tray before filling to make it easier to transfer. Bake at 160 C for 25 to 30 minutes until the filling is just set with a slight wobble in the very centre. Cool for at least 15 minutes before slicing. Serve warm or at room temperature.
